No lines inside the three assigned ranges are excluded for another owner: every line belongs to exactly one of the three packets below, confirmed by the validator's packet-partition-equals-assigned-union check.

(a) Export modal — DOM handle capture (11669-11678: `modal`, `fmtSel`, `rangeSel`, `scaleRow`, `scaleSel`, `sizeRow`, `wInput`/`hInput`, `alphaRow`, `progEl`, `runBtn`). `ALPHA_FORMATS=['png','prores']` (11684, a 5-line comment 11679-11683 explains: PNG sequence and ProRes 4444 both have a real alpha channel at the codec level; MP4/H.264 and GIF do not; TIFF/SVG/Lottie were out of scope rather than guessed). `NO_SCALE_FORMATS=['lottie','rive','ae-camera']` (11685, vector/keyframe-only export targets with no pixel-scale concept). `updateScaleVisibility()` (11686-11695): `scaleRow` hidden for any `NO_SCALE_FORMATS` value; `sizeRow` shown only when scale is NOT a no-scale format AND `scaleSel.value==='custom'`; `alphaRow` shown only for an `ALPHA_FORMATS` value; `#exp-rive-hint`/`#exp-ae-camera-hint` toggled per exact format match, each guarded for the element's own existence.

(b) Export modal — the desktop-only Rive gate: `gateDesktopOnlyFormats()` (11702-11717, an IIFE called once at module init) returns immediately if `window.__TAURI__!=='undefined'` is truthy (i.e. running inside the desktop app, where the gate is unnecessary); otherwise it disables the `option[value="rive"]` element, resets the select away from `rive` if it was already chosen, and — because this file loads BEFORE i18n.js, so `SM.t` would still return the raw key at this point — defers the label's own translated suffix (`' — '+SM.t('expAppOnly')`) into `window.SM.afterI18n`, i18n.js's documented escape hatch for exactly this ordering problem (11709-11712 comment), so the label re-picks the correct wording on every subsequent language switch too.

(c) Export modal — sizing math: W/H stay locked to the canvas' own aspect ratio (11723-11726 comment+code) — editing `wInput` recomputes `hInput` as `round(w*canvasH/canvasW)` and vice versa, a uniform scale multiplier rather than a crop/stretch control. `currentExportScale()` (11727-11733): for `scaleSel.value==='custom'`, returns `wInput.value/canvasW` (falling back to `canvasW` itself if the field is empty); otherwise parses `scaleSel.value` directly as a float percentage-style multiplier (e.g. `'0.5'`, `'2'`).

(d) Export modal — open/close chrome: `#btn-export` click (11735-11746) warns via `exportTauriOnly` only when NEITHER `SMExport.isAvailable()` NOR (if defined) `SMExport.videoBrowserAvailable()` is true, then calls `updateScaleVisibility()`, hides/clears the progress element, and shows the modal (`display:'flex'`). `#export-close` click and a click on the modal's own backdrop (`e.target===modal`) both hide it (11747-11748).

(e) Export modal — the async run handler (`#exp-run` click, 11750-11793): `saveAllLayerFrames()` first (flush any in-progress edit to persisted frame data); `range` resolves to `{start:0,end:totalFrames-1}` for `'all'` else `{start:waIn,end:waOut}` (work-area bounds); `scale` from `currentExportScale()`; `alpha` true only if the current format is in `ALPHA_FORMATS` AND `#exp-alpha` is checked; `state.exportIncludeShadowGuides=document.getElementById('exp-include-shadow').checked` (11759) is written DIRECTLY into state with no setter, no undo entry and no other mutation guard — the 4-line comment above it (11755-11758) explains this is deliberate: export.js's own `exportBuildFrame`/Lottie stroke filters both read `state.exportIncludeShadowGuides` directly, so this is the simplest way to reach both without threading a new parameter through every `exportXxx` function. `opts` (11760-11763) carries `start`,`end`,`scale`,`alpha`,`fps:state.fps`, plus three progress callbacks (`onProgress`→`exportRenderingFrame` templated with `{i}`/`{n}`; `onFfmpeg`→ raw ffmpeg stderr line truncated to 80 chars; `onRiveProgress`→ raw message). `runBtn.disabled=true` and `exportPreparing` shown before dispatch (11764); `fn` (11766) is looked up by format from a literal object mapping `svg/png/tiff/gif/mp4/prores/lottie/rive/ae-camera` to the corresponding `SMExport` method name; `await window.SMExport[fn](opts)` (11767) is the sole export call. Result branches (11768-11787): `res.cancelled`→`exportCancelled`; `res.ok`→`exportDone`, plus a format-specific `doneMsg` (`rive`→`exportRiveDone` with `{name}`; `ae-camera`→`exportAeCamMsg` with `{n}` PLUS an appended Kitsu-result suffix `exportAeCamKitsuOk`/`exportAeCamKitsuFail`; else→`exportGenericDone`), shown via `showToast`; a `lottie` success with `res.json` and `window.SMLottiePreview` present opens the Lottie preview INSTEAD of auto-closing (11780-11782, deliberately, per the 3-line comment 11777-11779: a bad export would otherwise be silent until opened elsewhere); every other successful format auto-closes the modal after a 900ms `setTimeout` (11784); a non-cancelled non-ok result shows `exportError` with `res.error||exportErrorUnknown` (11787). `catch`/`finally` (11788-11792): any thrown error shows `exportError` with the error's own `.message` or itself; `runBtn.disabled=false` always, regardless of outcome.

(f) The silent last-session restore (11810-11814): a 4-line lead-in comment explains the UX rationale (restored quietly into memory so the start screen's own 'Resume Last Session' card is instantly ready — a toast here would be confusing alongside the new start screen; state.js decides whether to actually SHOW that card, and surfaces its own confirmation once the user actually chooses it — cited by name only, not re-mapped). The code itself is one guarded statement: `try{var saved=localStorage.getItem('nemo-auto');if(saved)window.SM.importJSON(saved,true);}catch(e){}` — `importJSON`'s own second positional parameter is literally named `silent` at its declaration (timeline.js:2354, out of scope), confirming the `true` here means 'do not show the normal import UI/toast'.

(g) The right-panel collapse-to-rail feature, lead-in (11816-11821, 2026-08, quoting 'mettre en place le repli du panel droit en icon pour l'ui') explains WHY the collapsed state is a vertical label rail rather than a fixed icon set: up to 25 different `.psec` sections can be relevant depending on tool/selection (unlike a fixed panel dock), so a rail entry is built per CURRENTLY VISIBLE section from `updatePropsContext`'s own `show` object (timeline.js:3131, cited by name/line only). `renderPropsPanelRail(show)` (11822-11845): clears `#props-panel-rail`'s own innerHTML; for each `id` in `show` that is truthy, looks up the section element, reads its `.phdr` header text (stripping a leading `☰ ` glyph if present) as the label, skips silently if either the section or a non-empty label is missing, and builds a `<button class="rail-item">` whose click handler expands the panel (`togglePropsPanelCollapse(false)`), re-opens the section's own header if it was closed (`hdr.classList.contains('closed')` → `hdr.click()`), and scrolls it into view on the next animation frame. `window.renderPropsPanelRail=renderPropsPanelRail` (11845) is the cross-file/self-reentrant export (called again internally from `togglePropsPanelCollapse` itself, see (h)).

(h) `togglePropsPanelCollapse(force)` (11846-11872): `collapsed` resolves from the explicit `force` argument when given (`force!==undefined`), else toggles the panel's own current `.collapsed` class state. A 6-line comment (11850-11856) explains the width-persistence interaction: panel-width persistence (ui.js, out of scope) sets a plain inline `style.width`, which always wins over the `.collapsed` class's own CSS `width:36px` rule (inline beats any selector regardless of specificity) — so collapsing must explicitly clear the inline width first (stashing it on `window._propsExpandedWidth`, not a local var, so ui.js's own startup restore can prime the same value for the 'starts collapsed' case), and expanding must explicitly restore it. The resize handle (`#props-panel-resize`) is hidden while collapsed — dragging a 36px rail wider makes no sense. If collapsing AND a previous `show` object was cached (`window._lastPropsShow`), `renderPropsPanelRail` is invoked immediately so the rail reflects the panel's actual last-known context rather than staying empty until the next selection/tool change. `syncPropsPanelCollapseTitle()` is called unconditionally at the end (title text tracks collapsed state). The collapsed boolean persists to `localStorage['nemo-props-panel-collapsed']` (`'1'`/`'0'`), guarded in a `try`. `window.togglePropsPanelCollapse=togglePropsPanelCollapse` (11872) is the cross-file export the rail's own button (`#props-panel-collapse-btn`) and `initPropsPanelCollapse`'s own restore both reach.

(i) `syncPropsPanelCollapseTitle()` (11873-11883): an 8-line lead-in comment explains why this can't be a static `data-i18n-title` attribute — the title text is STATE-dependent (collapsed vs not) and i18n.js's own `[data-i18n-title]` sweep would blindly stomp it back to one fixed wording on every language switch, even while already collapsed; it is instead registered into `window.SM.afterI18n` (i18n.js's own documented escape hatch for exactly this class of problem) so a language switch re-picks the correct one of the two strings. The function itself guards on the button/panel/`window.SM`/`SM.t` all existing, then sets `btn.title=SM.t(panel.classList.contains('collapsed')?'expandPanelTitle':'collapsePanelTitle')`.

(j) `initPropsPanelCollapse`'s own remainder inside packet 3 (11889-11906, the IIFE's own head at 11884-11888 is C06's, see `reconciliation`): a 6-line comment (11889-11894) recounts a 2026-08-30 regression — the status bar and props-context labels are built with raw `innerHTML` from `SM.t` values rather than `data-i18n` attributes, so `applyI18n` cannot repaint them; at boot, before i18n.js has loaded, they are written from the placeholder `t` stub at the top of this file, which used to throw and now (with the placeholder) leaves raw untranslated keys visible ('thDrawDesc BthTool scAltDrag…', explicitly quoted as the measured string) until the next tool change. The fix registers a second `afterI18n` callback (11899-11901) that calls `updatePropsContext()` (if defined) once i18n has actually loaded, at the cost of one extra call of something the app already runs on every tool/selection change. `wasCollapsed` (11902-11903) is read from `localStorage['nemo-props-panel-collapsed']==='1'`, guarded in a `try`; if true, `togglePropsPanelCollapse(true)` runs the full collapse path (including an immediate rail render if `_lastPropsShow` is already set); otherwise `syncPropsPanelCollapseTitle()` alone sets the correct initial title for the already-expanded default state. `})();` (11906) closes the IIFE.

(k) Line 11907, the file's own final statement and literally its last line: `window.SM.setTool(state.userProfile&&state.userProfile.role==='producer'?'hand':'draw');updateUI();renderSymbolTabs();` — three calls in strict left-to-right order: `SM.setTool` (timeline.js:373, out of scope) picks the initial tool, `'hand'` for a `'producer'`-role user profile (a review-only role with no drawing intent) else `'draw'`; `updateUI()` (timeline.js:2727, out of scope) performs the app's first full UI paint; `renderSymbolTabs()` (timeline.js:6981, out of scope, C19v) builds the initial Component/symbol tab strip. This is, functionally, the timeline module's own 'main()' — the one statement guaranteed to run after every function/IIFE above it has been defined and every earlier IIFE (comment popover, text popover, combine panel, export modal, autosave interval, session restore, collapse-to-rail init) has already executed its own top-level body.

behavior: Lines 11679-11683 (comment, 5 lines): ALPHA_FORMATS rationale — PNG and ProRes 4444 have a real alpha channel; MP4/H.264 and GIF do not; TIFF/SVG/Lottie kept out of scope rather than guessed.

Lines 11686-11695 (code, 10 lines): `function updateScaleVisibility(){...}` — `scaleRow` hidden for a NO_SCALE_FORMATS value; `sizeRow` shown only for a scaled format with `scaleSel.value==='custom'`; `alphaRow` shown only for an ALPHA_FORMATS value; `#exp-rive-hint`/`#exp-ae-camera-hint` toggled per exact format, each guarded for existence.
